9 Full-Stack AI Projects Using Google
AI Studio and the Gemini API
A build guide for a 2nd-year B.Tech AI & Data Science student: ideas, architecture,
step-by-step plans and resume bullets.
How to use this guide
Each project follows the same pattern: React frontend, FastAPI (Python) backend, SQL database,
Gemini as the AI layer, and a live deployment. Using one stack across projects means you learn it
deeply once and reuse it. Pick two or three projects, not all nine. Depth beats volume on a resume.
Recommended picks
Security signal: Project 1 (Phishing Analyzer) or Project 3 (Prompt Injection Tester).
AI engineering signal: Project 5 (RAG Chatbot).
Product signal: Project 6 (Resume Matcher), the easiest to demo to recruiters.
Step 0: Shared setup (do this once)
1.Go to aistudio.google.com, sign in, and click Get API key. Prototype your prompts in the AI Studio
playground first, then click Get code to export a working snippet.
2.Install tools: Python 3.11+, Node.js 20+, Git, VS Code. Create a GitHub account if you do not have
one.
3.Create the folder layout below and run git init.
4.Store the key in a .env file and add it to .gitignore. Never commit an API key and never put it in
frontend code. The React app calls your backend, and only the backend calls Gemini.
5.Install backend packages: pip install fastapi uvicorn sqlalchemy python-dotenv
google-genai pydantic.
6.Create the frontend: npm create vite@latest frontend -- --template react.
Standard project layout
project/
  backend/
    app/
      main.py        # FastAPI app + routes
      gemini.py      # all Gemini calls live here
      models.py      # SQLAlchemy tables
      schemas.py     # Pydantic request/response models
      db.py          # engine + session

    .env             # GEMINI_API_KEY=...   (git-ignored)
  frontend/
    src/ (components, pages, api.js)

Project 1: Phishing Email and URL Analyzer
AI + Cybersecurity | Difficulty: Medium | Time: 2 to 3 weeks
Users paste an email or URL and get a risk score, the red flags found, and a plain-English explanation.
Under the hood you combine a classic ML classifier with Gemini and measure which approach is better.
The comparison is what makes this resume-worthy.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React with a paste box, risk meter, highlighted red flags, and a history page
Backend
FastAPI: POST /analyze, GET /history
Database
PostgreSQL or SQLite: scans(id, input_text, ml_score, llm_verdict, explanation, created_at)
AI / ML
scikit-learn (TF-IDF + Random Forest or Logistic Regression) plus Gemini for explanation
Deploy
Backend on Render, frontend on Vercel
Core features
Heuristic checks: URL length, IP-based hosts, suspicious TLDs, urgent language, mismatched link text
ML score from a model trained on a public phishing dataset (Kaggle or UCI)
Gemini returns JSON: verdict, confidence, list of red flags, safe advice
Scan history with filters and a chart of verdicts over time
How to build it, step by step
1.Download a labeled phishing dataset and split 80/20 into train and test.
2.Train TF-IDF + Logistic Regression and Random Forest. Record accuracy, precision, recall and F1 on
the test set. Save the model with joblib.
3.In AI Studio, write a system prompt that forces JSON output (verdict, confidence, red_flags[], advice).
Test it on 20 samples.
4.Build /analyze: run the heuristics and ML model, call Gemini, then merge the signals into one final
score.
5.Store every scan in the database. Add Pydantic validation and a length limit on input.
6.Build the React UI with a loading state, a colored risk gauge, and a red-flag list.
7.Evaluate on the held-out set: ML only vs Gemini only vs combined. Put the table in your README.
8.Deploy, add rate limiting, and write the README with screenshots.

Project 2: Log Anomaly Explainer
AI + Cybersecurity | Difficulty: Medium | Time: 2 to 3 weeks
Upload server or authentication logs. A statistical model flags suspicious events, and Gemini turns each
cluster of anomalies into an incident summary with recommended next steps, like a mini SOC assistant.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React dashboard: file upload, timeline chart (Recharts), incident cards
Backend
FastAPI: POST /upload, GET /incidents, GET /incidents/{id}
Database
PostgreSQL: log_events, incidents, incident_events (join table)
AI / ML
pandas + scikit-learn IsolationForest for detection; Gemini for summaries
Deploy
Docker Compose locally, then Render or Railway
Core features
Parser for common formats (SSH auth.log, Apache or Nginx access logs)
Features per IP and time window: failed-login count, request rate, unique paths, odd hours
IsolationForest anomaly score and grouping of related anomalies into incidents
Gemini summary: what happened, severity, likely cause, suggested action
How to build it, step by step
1.Get sample logs from public datasets (Loghub on GitHub) or generate fake auth logs with a script.
2.Write regex parsers that turn lines into structured rows (timestamp, ip, user, action, status).
3.Engineer features per 5-minute window and train an IsolationForest. Inspect the top anomalies by
hand.
4.Group anomalies from the same IP or window into one incident record.
5.Send each incident's events (capped at about 50 lines) to Gemini with a prompt that asks for severity
and next steps in JSON.
6.Build the dashboard: a timeline with anomalies marked, and a detail view per incident.
7.Inject known attacks (brute force, port scan) into test logs and measure how many are caught.
8.Containerize with Docker and deploy.
Stretch goals
Live log tailing with WebSockets
Map IPs to countries with GeoIP
Export incident reports as PDF
Sample resume bullet
Developed a log analysis platform (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) that detects brute-force and scanning
behavior with IsolationForest and generates LLM incident reports; detected X of Y injected attacks.

Project 3: Prompt Injection Tester and Defense Lab
AI + Cybersecurity | Difficulty: Medium | Time: 2 weeks
Build a deliberately vulnerable chatbot, then attack it with a library of prompt-injection and jailbreak
attempts and measure which defenses actually work. This is current, rare at your level, and ties both of
your interests together. Only test systems you built yourself.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React: chat window on one side, attack-results table and defense toggles on the other
Backend
FastAPI: POST /chat, POST /run-suite, GET /results
Database
SQLite or PostgreSQL: attacks, defenses, runs, results(attack_id, defense_id, success,
response)
AI / ML
Gemini as the target bot, plus Gemini as an automatic judge of whether an attack succeeded
Deploy
Vercel + Render
Core features
Target bot with a secret in its system prompt (for example, a fake discount code it must never reveal)
Attack library by category: direct override, role-play, encoding tricks, indirect injection via a document
Defense toggles: hardened system prompt, input filter, output filter, separate guard model
Automated run of every attack against every defense, and a success-rate matrix
How to build it, step by step
1.Read the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, especially LLM01 (Prompt Injection).
2.Build the target chatbot with a system prompt that contains a fake secret.
3.Write 30 to 50 test attacks in a JSON file, tagged by category.
4.Implement each defense as a separate function that wraps the chat call.
5.Write a judge prompt: given the attack, the response and the secret, did the bot leak it? Return true or
false.
6.Run the full suite (attacks x defenses) and store results.
7.Visualize a heatmap of attack category vs defense success rate.
8.Write a short findings section in the README: what worked, what failed, and why.
Stretch goals
Add a RAG target to test indirect injection through documents
Publish results as a blog post
Sample resume bullet
Designed a prompt-injection test harness with 40+ attacks across 4 categories; evaluated 4 defenses
and cut attack success from X% to Y%, documented against OWASP LLM Top 10.

Project 4: Secure Code Reviewer
AI + Cybersecurity | Difficulty: Medium | Time: 2 to 3 weeks
Paste code or connect a GitHub repo. A static scanner and Gemini together find likely vulnerabilities, map
them to OWASP categories or CWE IDs, and propose a fixed version with a diff.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React with Monaco editor, findings panel, side-by-side diff (react-diff-viewer)
Backend
FastAPI: POST /review, POST /review-repo, GitHub API via httpx
Database
PostgreSQL: reviews, findings(severity, cwe, line, explanation, fix)
AI / ML
Bandit (Python) or Semgrep for static analysis, Gemini for explanation and fixes
Deploy
Render (needs Bandit installed in the container)
Core features
Static scan first, then Gemini explains each finding in context
Severity ranking and CWE or OWASP mapping
Auto-generated fix with a unified diff
Review history and a security score per repo
How to build it, step by step
1.Collect intentionally vulnerable code: DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop snippets, or your own examples with
SQL injection, XSS and hardcoded secrets.
2.Run Bandit from Python with subprocess and parse its JSON output.
3.For each finding, send the surrounding 20 lines to Gemini and ask for explanation, CWE and a fix as
JSON.
4.Generate diffs with Python's difflib.
5.Build the editor UI with highlighted lines and a findings sidebar.
6.Add GitHub repo mode: fetch files through the API, scan only changed files.
7.Measure precision: how many flagged issues are real? Record false positives and compare with
Bandit alone.
8.Deploy and document the limitations honestly.
Stretch goals
GitHub Action that comments on pull requests
Support JavaScript through Semgrep rules
Sample resume bullet
Built a code security reviewer (React, FastAPI) combining Bandit with Gemini to explain and auto-fix
vulnerabilities; reduced false positives by X% over Bandit alone on N vulnerable samples.

Project 5: RAG Chatbot Over a Real Document Set
AI Engineering | Difficulty: Medium | Time: 2 to 3 weeks
A chatbot that answers questions from documents you upload (a college syllabus, research papers,
company policies) and cites the exact source passage. This is the most recognized AI-engineering project
employers look for.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React chat UI with file upload, streaming answers, and clickable source citations
Backend
FastAPI: POST /documents, POST /chat, GET /documents
Database
PostgreSQL for users, documents, chat history; ChromaDB or FAISS for vectors
AI / ML
Gemini embeddings + Gemini generation; pypdf for text extraction
Deploy
Render + Vercel (use a persistent disk or hosted Chroma)
Core features
PDF and text ingestion with chunking (500 tokens, 50 overlap)
Embedding each chunk and storing it with metadata (file, page)
Query: embed the question, retrieve top 4 chunks, and answer only from them
Citations shown under every answer, and a clear 'not found in documents' response
How to build it, step by step
1.Pick a document set you care about so you can judge answer quality (for example, your own syllabus
PDFs).
2.Extract text per page with pypdf and split into overlapping chunks.
3.Embed the chunks with the Gemini embedding model and store them in ChromaDB with file and page
metadata.
4.Write the chat endpoint: embed query, retrieve top-k, build a prompt that says 'answer only from the
context below, else say you do not know'.
5.Save chat sessions in SQL so the conversation persists.
6.Stream the answer to React and render citation chips.
7.Create 20 test questions with known answers. Measure accuracy, and compare chunk sizes or top-k
values.
8.Deploy and add per-user document isolation.
Key snippet (backend)
def answer(question, k=4):
    q_emb = embed(question)
    hits = collection.query(query_embeddings=[q_emb], n_results=k)
    ctx = "\n\n".join(f"[{m['file']} p.{m['page']}] {d}"
                       for d, m in zip(hits["documents"][0], hits["metadatas"][0

n_results=k)
    ctx = "\n\n".join(f"[{m['file']} p.{m['page']}] {d}"
                       for d, m in zip(hits["documents"][0], hits["metadatas"][0]))
    prompt = f"Answer ONLY from the context. If missing, say so.\n\n{ctx}\n\nQ: {question}"
    return ask(prompt), hits["metadatas"][0]

Hybrid search (BM25 + vectors)
Re-ranking step
Conversation memory with query rewriting

Project 6: Resume and Job-Description Matcher
AI Product | Difficulty: Easy to Medium | Time: 1 to 2 weeks
Upload a resume and paste a job description. The app extracts skills, scores the fit, lists the gaps, and
suggests rewritten bullets. It is easy to demo and recruiters instantly understand it.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React: two-panel upload, score ring, matched and missing skill chips, suggestions list
Backend
FastAPI: POST /match, GET /analyses, JWT login
Database
PostgreSQL: users, resumes, job_posts, analyses
AI / ML
Gemini structured extraction + sentence embeddings cosine similarity for the score
Deploy
Vercel + Render
Core features
PDF or DOCX resume parsing (pypdf, python-docx)
Skill extraction into JSON from both resume and job description
Match score = weighted mix of skill overlap and embedding similarity
Gap list and suggested bullet rewrites, with user accounts to save analyses
How to build it, step by step
1.Collect 10 real job descriptions in your target area and a few anonymized resumes.
2.Prompt Gemini to extract skills, tools, years of experience and education as JSON; test in AI Studio.
3.Compute embeddings for both texts and take cosine similarity.
4.Combine with exact skill overlap into one 0 to 100 score. Explain the formula in the README.
5.Add JWT authentication with FastAPI and password hashing (passlib/bcrypt).
6.Build the UI and store each analysis so users can compare versions.
7.Validate the score: do resumes you know are a better fit score higher?
Stretch goals
Cover letter generator
Browser extension for LinkedIn job pages
Sample resume bullet
Built a resume-JD matching web app (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) using Gemini skill extraction and
embedding similarity; scores correlated with manual fit rankings on N pairs.

Project 7: Data Analysis Assistant
Data Science | Difficulty: Medium | Time: 2 to 3 weeks
Upload a CSV and ask questions in plain English. Gemini writes pandas code, your backend runs it safely,
and the UI shows tables and charts. It showcases your DS skills inside a real full-stack app.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React: upload, schema preview, chat box, Plotly or Recharts output
Backend
FastAPI: POST /datasets, POST /ask
Database
PostgreSQL: datasets, questions, results (store the generated code for auditing)
AI / ML
Gemini code generation + pandas; restricted execution sandbox
Deploy
Render with resource limits
Core features
Automatic schema and summary stats on upload
Natural-language question to pandas code to result (table or chart spec)
Show the generated code so users can verify it
Saved analyses and chart export
How to build it, step by step
1.Pick 2 or 3 public datasets (Kaggle: Titanic, sales, IPL).
2.On upload, send only the column names, dtypes and 5 sample rows to Gemini (not the full data).
3.Prompt: 'Write one pandas expression or function that answers the question. Return JSON with code
and chart_type.'
4.Security step: never run raw model output with exec on your server. Run it in a subprocess with a
timeout, a restricted builtins dict, and an allowlist (only pandas and numpy imports). Reject code
containing os, sys, open, eval or __.
5.Return the result as JSON and render it in the frontend.
6.Test with 25 questions and record how often the answer is correct.
7.Deploy with memory and time limits.
Stretch goals
Auto-generated EDA report
Follow-up questions with context
Basic ML model training from chat
Sample resume bullet
Built a natural-language data analysis tool (React, FastAPI, pandas) with a sandboxed execution layer;
answered X% of 25 benchmark questions correctly across 3 datasets.

Project 8: Multimodal Receipt and Invoice Extractor
AI Product | Difficulty: Easy to Medium | Time: 1 to 2 weeks
Upload a photo or PDF of a bill. Gemini's vision capability returns structured JSON (vendor, date, items,
tax, total) which is saved to a database, shown in an editable table, and summarized in an expense
dashboard.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React: drag-and-drop upload, editable extracted table, monthly spend charts
Backend
FastAPI: POST /receipts, GET /expenses, GET /export.csv
Database
PostgreSQL: receipts, line_items, categories
AI / ML
Gemini multimodal (image and PDF input) with a JSON schema for output
Deploy
Vercel + Render, images in Cloudinary or local storage
Core features
Image or PDF upload with validation (type and size)
Structured extraction with a fixed JSON schema
Human-in-the-loop editing before saving
Auto-categorization, monthly dashboard and CSV export
How to build it, step by step
1.Collect 20 sample receipts (your own, with private details blurred).
2.In AI Studio, upload a receipt image and refine a prompt plus JSON schema until extraction is reliable.
3.Backend: read the uploaded bytes and send them to Gemini with the schema; validate the response
with Pydantic.
4.Save the receipt and line items in SQL tables with foreign keys.
5.Build the review screen where users correct mistakes.
6.Add dashboard charts: spend by category and by month.
7.Measure field-level accuracy (vendor, date, total) against your hand-labeled 20 receipts.
Stretch goals
Duplicate receipt detection
Budget alerts
Multi-currency support
Sample resume bullet
Built a receipt-processing app (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) using Gemini vision to extract structured
data; achieved X% field accuracy on 20 labeled receipts and automated monthly expense reporting.

Project 9: Study Assistant with Spaced Repetition
AI Product | Difficulty: Easy to Medium | Time: 2 weeks
Upload lecture notes and get flashcards and quizzes generated automatically. A spaced-repetition
scheduler (SM-2) decides what you review each day, and a dashboard tracks progress. It is a tool you will
genuinely use.
Full-stack architecture
Frontend
React: deck list, flashcard flip UI, quiz mode, streak and progress charts
Backend
FastAPI: POST /decks/generate, GET /review/today, POST /review/answer
Database
PostgreSQL: users, decks, cards(ease, interval, due_date), reviews
AI / ML
Gemini generates Q&A pairs and MCQs; SM-2 algorithm in plain Python
Deploy
Vercel + Render
Core features
Generate cards from PDF or pasted notes with a JSON schema
SM-2 scheduling: after each answer (0 to 5), update ease factor, interval and due date
Daily review queue and quiz mode
Stats: retention rate, cards due, streak
How to build it, step by step
1.Prompt Gemini to produce N flashcards (question, answer, difficulty) as JSON from a text chunk.
2.Implement SM-2: if quality < 3, reset interval to 1 day; else interval grows by the ease factor, and ease
updates by 0.1 - (5-q) x (0.08 + (5-q) x 0.02).
3.Store each card's ease, interval and due date; the daily queue is simply cards where due_date <=
today.
4.Build the flashcard UI with keyboard shortcuts.
5.Add quizzes (multiple choice generated by Gemini) and progress charts.
6.Add login so each user has their own decks, and deploy.
Stretch goals
Import Anki decks
Weak-topic detection
Mobile PWA
Sample resume bullet
Built a study platform (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) that auto-generates flashcards with Gemini and
schedules reviews with the SM-2 algorithm; used for N weeks across M decks.

Making any project resume-ready
Add one measurable result in the README and on the resume: accuracy, F1, latency, or attack
success rate.
Show the full stack: a live link, a GitHub repo with a clean commit history, and an architecture
diagram.
README checklist: problem statement, screenshots or a short GIF, tech stack, setup steps,
evaluation table, limitations, future work.
Do the unglamorous parts: input validation, error handling, rate limiting, secrets in environment
variables, and a few pytest tests for the backend.
Be honest about limits. Interviewers respect 'here is where it fails' far more than inflated claims.
Prepare to explain: why you picked each component, what you tried that did not work, and what you
would change next.
Suggested 8-week plan for two projects
Weeks
Focus
1
Step 0 setup, learn FastAPI basics, finish AI Studio prompt experiments for Project A
2 to 3
Backend and AI logic for Project A, database, tests
4
React frontend, deploy Project A, write README and evaluation
5
Start Project B: prompts, data and backend
6 to 7
Finish Project B frontend and evaluation
8
Polish both, record demo videos, update resume and LinkedIn, add GitHub pinned repos
